questoes.enunciado: What is the function of the cell at the tip of the arrow?

alternativas.feedback: Septal cells, one of the two cells lining the interalveolar septa, produce surfactant. Septal cells are more numerous than type I cells, although they do not cover nearly as much surface area as do type I cells. Septal cells divide to replensih both their own cell lline and type I cells.

alternativas.texto: Transport of oxygen and carbon dioxide

questoes.enunciado: Identify the passageway enclosed by the outline.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT: Respiratory bronchioles possess alveoli whose lumens are direcly contiguous with that of the respiratory bronchiole. Therefore, respiratory broncholes are capable of gaseous exchange and are part of the respiratory portion of the respiratory system.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the tissue indicated by the "X"s.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Patency of the trachea and primary bronchi is maintained by a series of hyaline cartilage rings. As bronchi decrease in diameter to become secondary bronchi, the rings are replaced by hyaline cartilage plates, as seen here. A perichondrium surrounds each plate.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the tissue indicated by the arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Olfactory epithelium (classified as pseudostratified columnar with cilia) of the olfactory region in the nose is much thicker than is respiratory epithelium, seen on the opposite surface. In addition to the usual epithelial cells, bipolar neurons are also present. Their nuclei are located in the middle of the epithelium with nuclei of supporting cells above and those of basal cells below the neuronal nuclei.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the passage indicated by the "X."

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. A secondary bronchus resembles a primary bronchus except that all layers are thinner; the passageway is surrounded by plates rather than rings of cartilage; and the smooth muscle becomes more prominent. Abundant, longitudinal elastic fibers remain in the lamina propria, but they are more dispersed than in the trachea and primary bronchi.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the passage in whose lumen the "X" is located.

alternativas.feedback: CORRRECT. Broncholes lack cartilage plates and mixed glands. In large bronchioles, such as the one seen here, the epithelium remains pseudostratified columnar with cilia and goblet cells; the lamina propria contains a smooth muscle layer represented as bands spiralling around the bronchiole. Other changes occur as the passageway decreases in diameter.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the entire structure shown in the right half of the image.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Many of the components of the interalveolar septum are shown. The attenuation of type I cell cytoplasm and the protrusion of the capillaries are most evident. Surfactant is not preserved during fixation of lung tissue, and no septal cells nor macrophages are present in this image.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the passage enclosed by the rectangle.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. An alveolar duct is formed as alveoli increase in number in a respiratory bronchiole, reducing the wall to a series of knobs. The knobs are really cross-sectional views of the rings that support the opening of the alveoli attached to them.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure in whose lumen the arrow is located.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Branches of bronchial arteries and veins travel within the respiratory passagways and, therefore, have to be smaller than the wall of the passageway they are supplying.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells at the tips of the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: The smallest bonchiole (terminal) is lined with a simple columnar with cilia and Clara cells (club cells), which are also present in the epithelium of respiratory bronchioles.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the layer indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Visceral pleura covers the exterior surface of the lung, lining the interior surface of the pleural cavity and sending septa into lung tissue proper. Pleura is composed of a mesothelium (simple squamous epithelium) and an underlying connective tissue containing elastic fibers and blood vessels.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the tissue identified by the arrows

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Smooth muscle reaches it greatest relative thickness in the bronchioles and is present as a meshwork of tissue embedded in the passageway. The contraction of the thick smooth muscle layer produced the folding typical in the lining of this passageway.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by an "X."

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The vocalis muscle is a band of skeletal muscle housed within the true vocal fold. The muscle regulates the tension of the fold, thus providing for the formation of different sounds.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures at the tips of the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. In the left image, numerous, longitudinally oriented elastic fibers, typical for the respiratory system, are dispersed in the lamina propria.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the layer at the tip of the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The epithelia of the conducting passageways of the respiratory system typically rest on a prominent basement membrane.
